new_statements.rule_in_words: Ilue, like all Lower Cross languages in Connell's sample, is a two-tone (H, L) terraced-level tone language with contrastive downstep; Connell finds no real evidence for word-level stress in Lower Cross (rejecting Ward's Efik verb-root stress and calling LC 'a non-stress language'), allowing only probable phrase-level stress and stress-like marking at compound junctures, which he says is uninvestigated except for Obolo.
new_statements.exceptions: Possible phrasal stress and stress marking at the juncture of compound-word elements (fn.32); Faraclas (1984a,b) posits an extra-high tone / phrase stress for Obolo only. Connell 1994:12 repeats that tone interacts with phrasal stress but is unstudied outside Obolo.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level statement for the Lower Cross languages (argued on Efik data, generalized to 'the other LC languages'); lexical tone described for citation forms; the only stress conceded is phrase-level. Nothing is said specifically about Ilue prosody beyond its inclusion in the group and (Connell 1994:10) its limited H-tone spreading.
new_statements.identity_note: The only first-hand statements are group-level: Connell 1991/1994 describe the prosody of the Lower Cross languages as a whole (19-22 languages, Ilue explicitly among those recorded by Connell in 1988 and named in the 1994 tone section); the argument against word stress is made on Efik data (Ward 1933) and generalized to 'Efik or the other LC languages'. Nothing Ilue-specific on prosody exists. Ilue is moribund/near-extinct: Udoh & Udoh 2022 report that by 2020 nobody in the Ilue community (Mbo LGA) claimed the language; all had shifted to Oro (oroo1241) and Efik.

sources.note: Ilue is one of the 19 LC languages studied (p.5; 1988 fieldwork p.14; consonant table p.41). Sec. 2.2.2 p.47: all LC languages are 'two-toned, terraced level languages' (H, L, downstep). pp.54-55: Ward's verb-root stress for Efik rejected, 'difficult to find any true evidence for stress'; fn.32 p.55: not asserting 'no stress at all in Efik or the other LC languages' -- likely phrasal stress and compound-juncture stress; fn.34 p.56 calls LC 'a non-stress language'. No word-stress rule for Ilue or any LC language.
